answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to periodically burn unique computational work anchored to scarce physical substrates, such as carving a private key into basalt that must be matched by a willow-branch sensor reading timber density variations. An attacker pays the full material and energy cost of fabricating and continuously validating each fake substrate, with no reuse across identities, so scaling sybils linearly multiplies the real-world expense without diminishing returns.
